[[Prime Prep Academy|Prime Prep]] ([[Dallas, Texas]]) | college = | draft_year = | career_start = 2014 | years1 = 2014–2015 | team1 = [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] | highlights = * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2014]]) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2014) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2014) * [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (2014) * 2x [[Texas Association of Private and Parochial Schools|TAPPS]] Class 4A State champion (2011–2012) }} '''Emmanuel Mudiay''' (born March 5, 1996) is a Congolese-American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). He committed to play for the [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball]] team on August 24, 2013 but later made the decision to forgo college and join a foreign professional team. Mudiay was rated as the second best recruit in his class by [[Rivals.com]] and award-winning sports columnist, [[Gary Parrish]]. The [[point guard]] is also listed as one of the top prospects for the [[2015 NBA draft]]. The Congo native played [[high school basketball]] for [[Grace Preparatory Academy]] and [[Prime Prep Academy]], where he gained much of the media's attention. == Early life == Mudiay was born on March 5, 1996 in [[Kinshasa]], [[Zaire]] to Jean-Paul Mudiay and Therese Kabeya. His father died when he was a toddler, and the family was tremendously troubled by the [[Second Congo War]]. He lived under the constant threat of the instability in the region, while his mother grew only enough coffee and vegetables to support their needs. In 2001, Kabeya and her sons sought asylum in the [[United States]] and eventually escaped.{{cite web|last1=Smith|first1=Corbett|title=Once endangered by African war, SMU signee Emmanuel Mudiay aims for NBA career|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sports/college-sports/smu-mustangs/20140308-once-endangered-by-african-war-smu-signee-emmanuel-mudiay-aims-for-nba-career.ece|work=DallasNews.com|date=March 8, 2014|accessdate=July 15, 2014}} He primarily spoke [[French language|French]] when arriving in the United States, but his younger brother said, "We felt like Americans." Mudiay began playing [[basketball]] in middle school and transformed into a talented [[point guard]]. == High school career == [[File:20140402 MCDAAG Emmanuel Mudiay tomahawk dunk (2).JPG|Mudiay dunking in the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]|thumb|left|upright]] In his freshman season, Mudiay attended [[Grace Preparatory Academy]] in [[Arlington, Texas]] where he played alongside [[Isaiah Austin]], who became an elite college [[Center (basketball)|center]] before being diagnosed with [[Marfan syndrome]]. Mudiay scored 16 points in the 2011 [[Texas Association of Private and Parochial Schools|TAPPS]] Class 4A Final, helping the team defeat two-time champions [[Westbury Christian School]] with the score of 42-37.{{cite web|last1=Smith|first1=Corbett|title=Basketball Player of the Year: Emmanuel Mudiay's rise has next stop at SMU|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sports/high-schools/boys-basketball-news/headlines/20140320-boys-poy.ece|work=DallasNews.com|date=March 20, 2014|accessdate=July 15, 2014}} Mudiay transferred to [[Prime Prep Academy]] in [[Dallas, Texas]] with head coach Ray Forsett for his final seasons in high school. The program was put under scrutiny following the ineligibility of Karviar Sheperd and [[Jordan Mickey]], two elite collegiate prospects. Upon excellent seasons with Prime Prep, however, Mudiay was rated the second-best recruit in his class by [[Rivals.com]]. He was also predicted to be a highly possible [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|number one]] pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]].{{cite web|last1=Payne|first1=Terrence|title=Top-5 recruit Emmanuel Mudiay will return to Prime Prep|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/07/23/top-5-recruit-emmanuel-mudiay-will-return-to-prime-prep/|work=NBCSports.com|date=July 23, 2013|accessdate=July 15, 2014}} He committed to play for the [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball]] team on August 24, 2013 because of the prospect of being coached by [[Larry Brown (basketball)|Larry Brown]], who previously won an [[List of NBA champions|NBA title]] with the [[Detroit Pistons]].[http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/23302984/smu-makes-statement-with-emmanuel-mudiays-commitment SMU makes statement with Emmanuel Mudiay's commitment] Mudiay selected the school over other possibilities with the likes of [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], and [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].{{cite web|title=Emmanuel Mudiay|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Emmanuel-Mudiay-120454|work=Yahoo.com|accessdate=July 15, 2014}} In the summer of 2014, Mudiay made the decision to forgo college and play overseas after considering playing in the [[Chinese Basketball Association]]. The move caused comparisons with [[Brandon Jennings]], who made a similar choice.{{cite web|last1=Gleeson|first1=Scott|title=Emmanuel Mudiay decides not to attend SMU, will turn pro overseas|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2014/07/14/emmanuel-mudiay-smu-decides-to-turn-pro-overseas/12634877/|work=USAToday.com|date=July 14, 2014|accessdate=July 15, 2014}}{{cite series 3-1.
